title: Orbit Logistics
summary: A subscription platform for freight-forwarding operations: web applications and backend services, backed by role-based access to operational data. Part of the Nativerse product ecosystem.
role: Founder and software engineer at Nativerse — product direction, architecture, implementation and production operations.
context:
Freight-forwarding operations span customers, shipments, internal staff, status updates and business data. In small operations that work usually lives across spreadsheets, chat and a handful of disconnected tools, which makes the same shipment mean different things to the person selling it and the person moving it.

Orbit is built inside Nativerse as a product rather than as one more per-client system: one subscription platform, web applications on top of backend services, and access scoped to the role of the person using it.

solution.title: One platform instead of per-client builds
solution.body: The product is offered as a subscription platform for freight-forwarding operations, so the operational model is shared and improved in one place rather than copied into every engagement.

solution.title: Web applications over backend services
solution.body: The customer-facing and internal workflows are web applications backed by dedicated services, which keeps business rules out of the interface and gives both surfaces the same answer.

solution.title: Role-based access to operational data
solution.body: Different people in a freight-forwarding business need different views of the same data. Access is modelled per role as part of the platform, not left to each screen to remember.

contribution: I founded Nativerse and lead Orbit's product direction, architecture, implementation and production operations. This page describes the product at the level the published CV supports; the implementation is not public while it is in development.
approach:
Orbit is a product bet, not a portfolio exercise: the same operational domain that HIT Cargo runs as a business is being turned into software other freight-forwarding businesses can subscribe to. That changes the constraints. A single-tenant tool can be shaped around one team's habits; a subscription platform has to make the workflow, the data model and the access rules explicit enough to survive a second and third customer.

The implementation is still in development. Rather than publish a feature inventory I cannot evidence, this page states what the product is and how it is positioned, and leaves the architectural detail to the moment there is a demo or code that can be shown safely.
confidentialityNote: Orbit is in development and has no public repository or demo. No module list, tenancy model, billing detail or customer is published here; those claims wait for implementation evidence or owner approval.
evidenceNote: Verified at the level of the published CV and the Nativerse role: a subscription platform for freight-forwarding operations with web applications, backend services and role-based data access. Deeper architecture is deliberately unpublished until it can be evidenced.
